samples.claim_anchored: Facility theft 4% H1 2023 → 19% H1 2024; average loss per incident $115,230 +83% YoY
samples.verification: CONFIRMED via PR Newswire press release from Overhaul. Figures confirmed by multiple trade press pickups (SecurityInfoWatch, DC Velocity, Food Logistics, Carrier Management). IMPORTANT: The source domain is prnewswire.com — this is a press release from Overhaul (vendor in the cargo security space), not a primary filing. Overhaul is both a vendor (cargo risk platform) and a research publisher. The report is Overhaul's own data product. This sits between secondary-press-release and secondary-trade. It does not meet auto-low-vendor criteria (Overhaul is not a company being claimed about in this context; it is providing third-party theft data). However it is a vendor-published press release, not an audited filing or government stat. Classified: secondary-press-release (Overhaul research arm). The 4%→19% trend figure is cited in draft as also sourced from BSI/TT Club (cross-validated for facility-theft direction). Score impact: Medium ceiling for this URL alone; claims using it alongside BSI/TT Club can reach High.

samples.claim_anchored: 70% commercial fleets do not share telematics with insurers; 79% never asked; 65% cite better rates when sharing
samples.verification: CONFIRMED figures exist at SambaSafety blog. However: verification of specific '70%' figure shows discrepancy. Web search returns SambaSafety GlobeNewswire press release (Oct 2025) stating '88% of fleets use telematics, but only 30% share data with insurers' — i.e., 70% NOT sharing. The draft's '70% do not share' figure is mathematically consistent with '30% share', so the 70% figure is correct as stated. The 79% 'never asked' figure confirmed. The 65% 'better rates' figure confirmed. SOURCE CATEGORY: SambaSafety is a vendor (fleet telematics risk intelligence platform). The blog at sambasafety.com is classified as auto-low-vendor for claims about SambaSafety's own product, but this data is a fleet survey result about industry behavior — not a claim about SambaSafety's own capability. Classify as secondary-trade / vendor-sponsored research. Not auto-low, but also not primary. Single source for a key operating-behavior statistic. Override triggered: single-domain (only SambaSafety for this figure). Score: Low — single vendor-sponsored source for a critical market behavior claim.

samples.claim_anchored: Indonesia mandatory ePOD Q3 2026, targeting IDR 2.1 trillion ($130M) annual fraud losses
samples.verification: CRITICAL FAILURE. Web search for 'Indonesia ePOD mandatory Q3 2026 IDR 2.1 trillion electronic proof delivery regulation' returns ZERO government or regulatory sources confirming this mandate. The cfglobal.co domain is an industry blog (CF Global — a logistics consultancy marketing blog). No BPS Indonesia, Ministry of Transportation Indonesia, or Kemenhub regulation mandating ePOD by Q3 2026 was found in any search. The IDR 2.1 trillion figure is unverified and not traceable to any government source. This is a single trade/industry blog source for a regulatory fact that would need a Kemenhub (Ministry of Transportation) gazette or BPS publication to be credible. Auto-Low: single industry blog, no government corroboration, regulatory fact unverified. Score: Low. Flag as HIGH PRIORITY for deep research.

gate_reasoning: Stage 5 scores 24% High, 13% Medium, and 63% Low across 46 scored claims — well below the QUALITY-BAR.md target of ≤30% Low and ≥25% High. The 63% Low rate is driven by three structural problems. First, the entire facility-theft trend narrative (4%→19%→37% across H1 2023, H1 2024, Q2 2025) rests on Overhaul's proprietary data series with no independent validation from CargoNet, NICB, or any government source — this is the most consequential single-vendor dependency in the document. Second, the Indonesia mandatory ePOD claim (Q3 2026, IDR 2.1 trillion) is sourced from a single industry blog with no government corroboration found in any search; if this regulation does not exist or is mischaracterized, it removes the only government-anchor for the POD pain point in SEA. Third, all Mexico cargo theft quantification (24,000 incidents, $368M losses, 83.8% violence, state breakdown) traces back to Overhaul as the single originating source, despite the user concern note about 'Mexico SCT figures' — no Mexican government source (SCT, SSPC, Guardia Nacional) was located or cited. The five high-priority deep-research targets are: (1) Indonesia ePOD Kemenhub regulation verification, (2) independent validation of the 4%→19%→37% Overhaul facility-theft trend, (3) Mexico government cargo crime statistics (SSPC/Guardia Nacional), (4) NTC&Logistica primary publication for Brazil hijacking type breakdown, and (5) SambaSafety telematics non-sharing survey independent corroboration. The High-scoring claims (ATRI, CargoNet, BSI/TT Club, Securitas AR2024, Samsara 10-K, TIA, PowerFleet IR, Motorola Solutions IR) provide a credible structural skeleton, but the quantified cost and frequency figures for the three core pain points (facility theft, paper POD, LATAM escort) require deep-research passes before the stage is shippable at WP grade.
